questions.question: Chords AB and CD of a circle intersect externally at P. If AB = 7 cm, CD = 1 cm and PD = 5 cm, then 50% of the length of PA (in cm) is:
questions.solution:
**Given data:**

AB = 7 cm

CD = 1 cm

PD = 5 cm

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8e67eb472bdf2b59920e92a3b2a2a36f73ef411461d740965b078ef5121833f2.png] 

From the basic proportionality theorem,

PB × PA = PD × PC

Substituting the values-

⇒ PB × (7 + PB) = 5 × (5 + 1)

⇒ PB × (7 + PB) = 5 × 6 = 30

⇒ PB² + 7PB -30 = 0

⇒ PB2 + 10PB - 3PB -30 = 0

⇒ PB × (PB + 10) - 3 × (PB + 10) = 0

⇒ (PB - 3) × (PB + 10) = 0

Either PB = 3 or -10 (PB cannot be negative. Hence, PB = 3)

∴ PA = AB + BP = 7 + 3 = 10

Now,

⇒ 50% of PA = 50 × 10/100 = 5

∴ **The value of 50% PA is 5 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__** The equation PB × (7 + PB) = 30 could be solved by breaking 30 into appropriate factors to match the equation PB × (7 + PB).

⇒ 30 = 10 × 3 and 10 = 7 + 3

∴ 30 = 3 × (7 + 3)

⇒ PB × (7 + PB) = 3 × (7 + 3)

∴ PB = 3 cm and PA = 10 cm

⇒ 50% of PA = 50 × 10/100 = 5

∴ The value of 50% PA is 5 cm.

questions.question: AB and AC are tangents to a circle with centre O from an external point A. The tangents AB and AC touch the circle at B and C, respectively, such that ∠BAC = 118°. Find the measures of ∠OCB.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For tangents **AB** and **AC** drawn from an external point **A** to a circle with centre **O**, the angle **∠OCB** is always exactly half of the vertex angle **∠BAC**.

Logic: ∠OCB = ∠BAC ÷ 2

⇒ ∠OCB = 118° ÷ 2

⇒ ∠OCB = 59°

**∴ The correct answer is 59°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** ∠BAC = 118° and tangents AB, AC.

**Formula Used:** Sum of angles in quadrilateral = 360°; Tangent ⊥ Radius property; Isosceles triangle property.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4eeb2d6b5c03a95a39eedb46cc0f82baa6dd12ff98f0fee70c2fb75722dd7ff6.png] 

In quadrilateral **ABOC**:

⇒ ∠ABO = ∠ACO = 90° (Radius is perpendicular to the tangent at point of contact)

⇒ ∠BAC + ∠ABO + ∠BOC + ∠ACO = 360°

⇒ 118° + 90° + ∠BOC + 90° = 360°

⇒ ∠BOC = 360° − 298° = 62°

In triangle **OBC**:

⇒ **OB = OC** (Radii of the same circle)

⇒ ∠OBC = ∠OCB (Angles opposite to equal sides are equal)

⇒ ∠BOC + ∠OBC + ∠OCB = 180°

⇒ 62° + 2 × ∠OCB = 180°

⇒ 2 × ∠OCB = 180° − 62° = 118°

⇒ ∠OCB = 59°

**∴ The correct answer is 59°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Tangent Properties

Tangents from an external point to a circle are equal in length (AB = AC) and subtend equal angles at the centre.

Supplementary Angles

The angle between two tangents and the angle subtended by the radii at the centre are supplementary (∠BAC + ∠BOC = 180°).

Alternative Segment Theorem

The angle between a tangent and a chord through the point of contact is equal to the angle in the alternate segment.</p

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ce789db896f06a5046a2de0d89b37d99ee2f9d0239ef220f422d1bc32335f60a.png] 

The angle subtended by an arc at the centre is double the angle subtended by it at any point on the remaining part of a circle.

⇒ External ∠AOB = 2∠ ACB

⇒ External ∠AOB = 115° × 2 = 230°

⇒ Internal ∠AOB = 360° - 230° = 130°

In ΔABO, AO = BO = Radii of circle.

In ΔABO,

⇒ ∠BAO + ∠ ABO + ∠ AOB = 180°

⇒ ∠BAO = 1/2 × (180° - 130°) = 25°

**∴ ∠OAB = 25°.**

questions.question: From a point P which is at a distance of 10 cm from the centre O of a circle of radius 6 cm, a pair of tangents PQ and PR to the circle at point Q and R, respectively, are drawn. The area of the quadrilateral PQOR is equal to

In △OQP

questions.question: Points A and B are on a circle with center O. PAM and PBN are tangents to the circle at A and B respectively from a point P outside the circle. Point Q is on the major arc AB such that ∠QAM = 58° and ∠QBN = 50°, then find the measure (in degrees) of ∠APB.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

∠QAM = 58°

∠QBN = 50°

**Concept used:**

The angles of an alternate segment subtended by a tangent to a circle are equal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/96d35ab96232e2e0178d1a0988052a7a515bd864d595ea90b4e2c096877cf758.png] 

∠APM = ∠PNM and ∠BPN = ∠PMN

Alternate line segment theorem

cyclic quadrilateral theorem = The sum of a pair of opposite angles is 180° (supplementary)

**Calculation:**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/47e82173d61a833d56f69add8efdbb7172c5308f80ec04ff3d6f37913afa9a81.png] 

The angles of an alternate segment subtended by a tangent to a circle are equal.

∠QAM = ∠ABQ = 58°

∠QBN = ∠BAQ = 50°

So, ∠AQB = 72° 

∠BOA = 2∠AQB = 2 × 72° = 144° 

In quadrilateral PBOA,

∠APB + ∠BOA = 180° (because OB ⊥ PN & OA ⊥ PM)

⇒ ∠APB = 180 - 144

⇒ ∠APB = 36°

**∴ The measure of ∠APB is 36°**

questions.question: In two circles centred at O and O’, the distance between the centres of both circles is 17 cm. The points of contact of a direct common tangent between the circles are P and Q. If the radii of both circles are 7 cm and 15 cm, respectively, then the length of PQ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given:

The Radii of the two circles are 7 cm and 15 cm

The distance between their centres is 17 cm.

Formula used:

Length of direct common tangent = sqrt {D² - (r₁ - r₂)²} 

Where D = Distance between their centers, r1 = radius of the bigger circle and r2 = radius of the smaller circle

Calculation:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/726975bbefbb6bc401e04d6b4c972ebcce6acec738379596570646b2b5bc2185.png] 

According to the formula,

Length of PQ = sqrt {17² - (15 - 7)²}

⇒ Length of PQ = sqrt {289 - 64}

⇒ Length of PQ = 15 cm

∴ The length of the direct common tangent is 15 cm.

questions.question: What is the length (in cm) of the transverse common tangent between two circles with radii 6 cm and 4 cm, given that the distance between their centres is 14 cm?
questions.solution:

The Radii of the two circles are 6 cm and 4 cm

The distance between their centers is 14 cm

**Formula Used:**

Transverse common tangent = sqrt {D²-(R+r)²}

Where D is the distance between the centers of the two circles

' R ' and ' r ' are the respective radii of the circles

**Calculation:**

We know that, D = 14 cm, R = 6 cm and r = 4 cm

According to the formula,

Transverse common tangent = sqrt{14²-(6+4)²} = √96 = 4√6 cm

**∴ The correct answer is option 2**

questions.question: A chord 21 cm long is drawn in a circle of diameter 25 cm. The perpendicular distance of the chord from the centre is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Radius** (r) = 25 ÷ 2 = 12.5 cm

Half of the **chord** (a) = 21 ÷ 2 = 10.5 cm

Using the **Pythagorean relation** for the **perpendicular distance** (d):

⇒ d = √(r² − a²)

⇒ d = √(12.5² − 10.5²)

⇒ d = √((12.5 − 10.5) × (12.5 + 10.5)) = √(2 × 23) = √46 cm

**∴ The correct answer is √46 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Diameter** of the circle = 25 cm

Length of the **chord** = 21 cm

**Formula Used:**

**Radius** (r) = **Diameter** ÷ 2

The **perpendicular** drawn from the centre of a circle to a chord bisects the chord.

In a **right-angled triangle**, by **Pythagoras theorem**: Hypotenuse² = Base² + Perpendicular²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a15536eb57cbd2165e9577777654cfdc2398472e789e84633dfca39f2545c9aa.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let O be the centre of the circle and AC be the chord of length 21 cm.

Let OM be the perpendicular from the centre O to the chord AC.

⇒ **Radius** of the circle (OA) = 25 ÷ 2 = 12.5 cm

⇒ Since OM is perpendicular to AC, it bisects AC.

⇒ AM = MC = AC ÷ 2 = 21 ÷ 2 = 10.5 cm

In **right-angled triangle** OMA, by **Pythagoras theorem**:

⇒ OA² = OM² + AM²

⇒ 12.5² = OM² + 10.5²

⇒ 156.25 = OM² + 110.25

⇒ OM² = 156.25 − 110.25

⇒ OM² = 46

⇒ OM = √46 cm

**Option Evaluation:**

Option (1) √41 is incorrect because 12.5² − 10.5² = 46, not 41.

Option (2) √23 is incorrect because the square of the distance is 46, not 23.

Option (3) √56 is incorrect because 156.25 − 110.25 = 46, not 56.

Option (4) √46 is correct as it perfectly satisfies the Pythagorean relation OM = √46 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is √46 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perpendicular Bisector Theorem

The perpendicular drawn from the centre of a circle to a chord always bisects the chord into two equal halves.

Pythagoras Theorem

In any right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two sides: Hypotenuse² = Base² + Height².

Chord Length Formula

The length of a chord can be calculated as 2 × √(r² − d²), where r is the radius and d is the perpendicular distance from the centre.</p

questions.question: The sides AB, BC and AC of ΔABC are 12 cm, 8 cm and 10 cm, respectively. A circle is inscribed in the triangle touching AB, BC and AC at D, E and F, respectively. The ratio of the lengths of AD to CE is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The sides AB, BC and AC of ΔABC are 12 cm, 8 cm and 10 cm.

A circle is inscribed in the triangle touching AB, BC and AC at D, E and F.

**Concept Used:**

Length of tangents from a fixed point outside the circle is always same.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/573f6cebf0f4bfe3d26b584956f449cd063109283a9bc2bad77959482a5abf93.png] 

Let length of AD = AF = x

Length of BD = BE = y

And length of CE = CF = z

Now,

2 × (x + y + z) = (12 + 8 + 10)

⇒ x + y + z = 15

Again,

AB = (x + y) = 12 cm

BC = (y + z) = 8 cm

CA = (x + z) = 10 cm

Now, x = (x + y + z) – (y + z) = 15 – 8 = 7 cm

z = (x + y + z) – (x + y) = 15 – 12 = 3 cm

AD : CE = 7 : 3

**∴ Ratio of the lengths of AD to CE is 7 : 3**

questions.question: If two tangents to a circle of radius 3 cm are inclined to each other at angle of 60°, then the length of each tangent is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Two tangents to a circle of radius 3 cm are inclined to each other at angle of 60°

**Concept used:**

An external point's tangents to a circle are equal.

SSS congruency criterion

Tan 30° trignometric ratio = 1/√3

**Calculations:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7f96235eea3435c132300b1f21278d8243aa56a6de9776b43ef3a4629de76e9b.png] 

Let AP and CP be the tangents drawn to a circle

According to the question,

∠CPA = 60°

So, AP = CP

In triangle PAO and triangle PCO,

⇒ AP = CP

⇒ AO = CO = radius of circle

⇒ PO = PO = common side

Triangle PAO and triangle PCO are similar, by SSS criterion, 

At the point of contact the radius of a circle is perpendicular to the tangent

So, ∠PAO = ∠PCO = 90°

Since AO = CO = radius

⇒ ∠PAO = ∠PCO

⇒ ∠CPA = ∠OPA + ∠OPC

⇒ 2∠OPA = 60°

⇒ ∠OPA = 60°/2

⇒ ∠OPA = 30°

In triangle PAO,

PAO is a right triangle with A at right angle.

⇒ tan 30° = AO/PA

⇒ 1/√3 = 3/AP

⇒ AP = 3√3 cm

**∴ The length of each tangent is 3√3 cm.**

questions.question: If the length of a chord of a circle, that makes an angle of 60° with the tangent drawn at one end point the chord, is 8√3 cm, then the radius of the circle will be:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The length of a chord of a circle = 8√3 cm

**Concept used:**

The tangents drawn at the ends of a chord of a circle make equal angles with the chord.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0f0682bfe4e97dea50b8416956be4bb483bf98694e8bc5d18ed354b8288d69b9.png] 

If a perpendicular is drawn from O to AB, then it will touch AB at M

So, length of AM = 8√3 ÷ 2 = 4√3

Now, in ΔAOM

∠AOM = 60° [The tangents drawn at the ends of a chord of a circle make equal angles with the chord]

So, Sin 60° = AM/OA

⇒ √3/2 = 4√3/OA

⇒ 1/2 = 4/OA

⇒ OA = 2 × 4

⇒ 8 cm

**∴ Length of radius is 8 cm**

questions.question: In a circle, AB and DC are two chords. When AB and DC are produced, they meet at P. If PC = 2.8 cm, PB = 3.15 cm and AB = 3.85 cm, then CD = ?
questions.solution:
Given:

AB and DC are two chords. They are produced to meet at P.

PC = 2.8 cm, PB = 3.15 cm and AB = 3.85 cm,

Concept used:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d6d2eace4999d85a1e022b4b9172b827bc52a10dc9e1d57dc1ea1f75257e4a3c.png] 

Here, PA & PC are two secants and PT is a tangent at point T on the circle. 

So, we know,

PA × PB = PC × PD = (PT)2

Calculation:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/981f82cfabd8a424edec58181eea3df766652ede6a5018b9a524238352c25ef1.png] 

So, PA = AB + PB = 3.15 + 3.85 = 7 cm

Now,

PA × PB = PD × PC

⇒ 7 × 3.15 = PD × 2.8 

⇒ PD = 7.875

⇒ PC + CD = 7.875

⇒ CD = 5.075

**∴ The length of CD is 5.075 cm.**

questions.question: In a circle with center O and radius 13 cm, a chord AB is drawn. Tangents at A and B intersects at P such that ∠APB = 60°. If the distance of AB from the center O is 5 cm, then what is the length (in cm) of AP?

OA = 13 (given)

Using Pythagoras theorem

AM = 12

questions.question: Sum of the angles made by a chord at the centre and on the major arc of a circle is 180 degree. What will be the angle made at the centre of the circle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The ratio of the angle at the **center** to the angle on the **major arc** (circumference) is always 2 : 1.

Total parts = 2 + 1 = 3 units.

Given 3 units = 180°

1 unit = 60°

Angle at the **center** = 2 units = 2 × 60° = 120°.

**∴ The correct answer is 120 degree.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Sum of the angles made by a chord at the center and on the major arc is 180°.

**Formula Used:** The angle subtended by an **arc** (or chord) at the **center** is double the angle subtended by it at any point on the **major arc** (remaining part of the circle).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0ef1e5a46cb6c98c6616658934f993d12e63fbbd8ee4c66514b3ae4cd567424b.png] 

Let the angle made on the **major arc** be x.

According to the theorem, the angle at the **center** will be 2x.

⇒ 2x + x = 180°

⇒ 3x = 180°

⇒ x = 180° ÷ 3

⇒ x = 60°

Now, the angle at the **center** of the circle:

⇒ 2x = 2 × 60°

⇒ 2x = 120°

**∴ The correct answer is 120 degree.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle in a Semicircle

The angle subtended by a diameter at any point on the circumference is always 90°.

Cyclic Quadrilateral Property

The sum of the opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral is always 180°.

Angles in the same segment

Angles subtended by the same arc at any point on the remaining part of the circle are equal.</p

questions.question: The distance between the centres of the two circles, with radii 3 cm and 2 cm, respectively, is 13 cm. The length (in cm) of a transverse common tangent is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The distance between the centers of the two circles, with radii 3 cm and 2 cm, respectively, is 13 cm.

**Formula Used:**

Length of transverse common tangent = sqrt{d² - (r₁ + r₂)²} 

Where,

d = distance between the centres of the two circles

r₁ = radius of the first circle

r₂ = radius of the second circle

**Calculation:**

d = 13 cm

r₁ = 3 cm

r₂ = 2 cm

⇒ Length of transverse common tangent = sqrt{13² - (3 + 2)² } 

⇒ Length of transverse common tangent = sqrt{169 - 25} 

⇒ Length of transverse common tangent = sqrt{144} 

⇒ Length of transverse common tangent = 12 cm

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**

questions.question: Two circles having radii 12 cm and 8 cm, respectively, touch each other externally. A common tangent is drawn to these circles which touch the circles at M and N, respectively. What is the length (in cm) of MN?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For two circles touching **externally**, the length of the **direct common tangent** is:

**MN = 2 √(R × r)**

⇒ MN = 2 √(12 × 8) = 2 √96

⇒ MN = 2 × 4√6 = 8√6 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 8√ 6 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of the first circle (R) = 12 cm

Radius of the second circle (r) = 8 cm

The circles touch each other **externally**.

**Formula Used:**

Length of **direct common tangent** (MN) = √[d² − (R − r)²]

Where **d** is the distance between the **centers** of the circles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a325dc4f7bf14aa3d5ed38fd72dd3eb21d46790fa6353386f9d5085f086de385.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Since the circles touch **externally**, the distance between centers (d) = R + r

⇒ d = 12 + 8 = 20 cm

⇒ MN = √[20² − (12 − 8)²]

⇒ MN = √[400 − 4²]

⇒ MN = √[400 − 16] = √384

⇒ MN = √(64 × 6) = 8√6 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 8√ 6 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Common Tangent (DCT)

The length of the direct common tangent is given by √[d² − (R − r)²], where d is the distance between centers.

Transverse Common Tangent (TCT)

The length of the transverse common tangent is given by √[d² − (R + r)²]. It exists only if d > R + r.

Touching Externally vs Internally

For **externally** touching circles, d = R + r. For **internally** touching circles, d = |R − r|.</p

questions.question: Two circles with centres O and P and radii 17 cm and 10 cm, respectively, intersect each other at A and B. The length of the common chord AB is 16 cm. What is the perimeter of the triangle OAP (in cm)?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The **common chord** AB is bisected by the line of centres OP at M, so AM = 8 cm.

Using **Pythagorean triplets** for right-angled triangles ΔAMO and ΔAMP:

For ΔAMO (hypotenuse 17, leg 8): OM = √(17² − 8²) = 15 cm.

For ΔAMP (hypotenuse 10, leg 8): PM = √(10² − 8²) = 6 cm.

Distance between centres OP = OM + PM = 15 + 6 = 21 cm.

Perimeter of ΔOAP = OA + AP + OP = 17 + 10 + 21 = 48 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 48 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of first circle (centre O), OA = 17 cm

Radius of second circle (centre P), PA = 10 cm

Length of **common chord**, AB = 16 cm

**Formula Used:**

The line joining the centres of two intersecting circles is the **perpendicular bisector** of their common chord.

**Pythagoras Theorem:** Hypotenuse² = Base² + Perpendicular²

Perimeter of triangle = Sum of all three sides

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/826178678a41af1ac856d119e6f9dd69f022f769c43bbe26bea14b00b5658229.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the line joining the centres O and P intersect the common chord AB at point M.

⇒ AM = MB = AB ÷ 2

⇒ AM = 16 ÷ 2 = 8 cm

Since OP is perpendicular to AB, ΔAMO and ΔAMP are **right-angled triangles** at M.

In right-angled ΔAMO, using Pythagoras theorem:

⇒ OA² = OM² + AM²

⇒ 17² = OM² + 8²

⇒ 289 = OM² + 64

⇒ OM² = 289 − 64 = 225

⇒ OM = √225 = 15 cm

In right-angled ΔAMP, using Pythagoras theorem:

⇒ PA² = PM² + AM²

⇒ 10² = PM² + 8²

⇒ 100 = PM² + 64

⇒ PM² = 100 − 64 = 36

⇒ PM = √36 = 6 cm

Now, the distance between the centres OP is:

⇒ OP = OM + PM

⇒ OP = 15 + 6 = 21 cm

We need to find the **perimeter** of ΔOAP:

⇒ Perimeter of ΔOAP = OA + AP + OP

⇒ Perimeter of ΔOAP = 17 + 10 + 21 = 48 cm

**Why other options are incorrect:**

⇒ **Option (1) 40 cm:** This value does not correspond to any valid geometric configuration of the given circles.

⇒ **Option (3) 25 cm:** This is incorrect as the sum of the two radii alone is 17 + 10 = 27 cm, so the perimeter of the triangle must be greater than 27 cm (since OP > 0).

⇒ **Option (4) 33 cm:** This does not match either of the mathematically possible perimeters (48 cm or 36 cm) derived from the circle properties.

**∴ The correct answer is 48 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Perpendicular Bisector Property

The line segment connecting the centres of two intersecting circles is always the perpendicular bisector of their common chord.

Alternative Case (Centres on Same Side)

If the centres of the circles lie on the same side of the common chord, the distance between the centres is OP = OM − PM = 15 − 6 = 9 cm. In this case, the perimeter of ΔOAP would be 17 + 10 + 9 = 36 cm.

Pythagorean Triplets

Common integer right-triangle side sets like (8, 15, 17) and (6, 8, 10) help solve competitive exam geometry questions extremely quickly without full calculation.</p

questions.question: O is the centre and the arc PQR subtends an angle of 240° at O. PQ is extended to A. Then ∠AQR is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Angle subtended by **major arc PQR** at **centre O** = 240°

Angle subtended by the same arc at **circumference** (say ∠PSR) = 240° ÷ 2 = 120°

In a **cyclic quadrilateral**, the **exterior angle** is equal to the **interior opposite angle**.

Since **PQ** is extended to **A**, the exterior angle ∠AQR = interior opposite ∠PSR.

⇒ ∠AQR = 120°

**∴ The correct answer is 120°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Centre of circle = **O**

Angle subtended by **arc PQR** at O = 240°

**PQ** is extended to point **A**.

**Property used:**

1. The angle subtended by an arc at the centre is double the angle subtended by it at any point on the remaining part of the circle.

2. The sum of opposite angles of a **cyclic quadrilateral** is 180°.

3. **Exterior angle** of a cyclic quadrilateral is equal to the **interior opposite angle**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/584ae4ab1df3f4f219fdd404ab564b1b32706eb6540158b44221c14c0dd59811.png] 

Let **S** be any point on the minor arc **PR**.

⇒ Reflex ∠POR = 240° (Angle subtended by arc PQR at centre)

⇒ ∠PSR = 1/2 × Reflex ∠POR

⇒ ∠PSR = 1/2 × 240° = 120°

Now, **PQRS** is a **cyclic quadrilateral** because all four vertices lie on the circle.

⇒ ∠PQR + ∠PSR = 180° (Opposite angles of cyclic quadrilateral)

⇒ ∠PQR = 180° − 120° = 60°

Since **PQA** is a straight line (extension of PQ):

⇒ ∠PQR + ∠AQR = 180° (Linear pair)

⇒ ∠AQR = 180° − 60° = 120°

**∴ The correct answer is 120°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle at Centre Theorem

The angle subtended by an arc at the center is exactly double the angle subtended by the same arc at any point on the circumference of the circle.

Cyclic Quadrilateral Exterior Angle

The exterior angle formed by extending one side of a cyclic quadrilateral is always equal to the interior opposite angle of the quadrilateral.

Opposite Angles Property

In any cyclic quadrilateral, the sum of a pair of opposite angles is always 180° (supplementary angles).</p

questions.question: In a circle, AB and CD are two diameters which are perpendicular to each other. Find the length of chord AC.
questions.solution:
**GIVEN:**

Diameters = AB and CD 

Diameters are perpendicular to each other.

**CONCEPT USED:**

Diameters are perpendicular = they make 90 degree angle with each other

Radius = Diameter/2 and radius of the circle are always equal.

In a right angled triangle ,

H² = P² + B² 

Where, H = Hypotenuse, P = perpendicular, B = Base.

**CALCULATIONS :**

Now, we are given a circle with centre O and two perpendicular diameters AB and CD respectively.

We , need to find the length of chord i.e. AC 

We have the following corresponding figure as following,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ac61a8ba40727f04034968e8a0f602e9ff04b5bf94cd8fcdd3ab16847e9988fe.png] 

Since AB = CD ( Diameters of the same circle are equal )

Also, ∠ AOC = 90° and AO = AB/2 

Here AO = OC ( As both are radius)

Now, Join A and C, so that Right triangle AOC is formed.

Now, in triangle AOC with ∠ AOC = 90 degree

AC² = OA² + OC²

⇒ AC² = OA² + OA²

⇒ AC² = (AB/2)² + (AB/2)²

⇒ AC² = AB²/2 

⇒ AC = ABover sqrt2

**Hence, Length of the chord is **ABover sqrt2**.**

questions.question: In a circle with centre O, AB and CD are parallel chords on the opposite sides of a diameter. If AB = 12 cm, CD = 18 cm and the distance between the chords AB and CD is 15 cm, then find the radius of the circle (in cm).
questions.solution:
**Given:**

AB = 12 cm

CD = 18 cm

Distance between the chords AB and CD = 15 cm

**Formula used:**

AB² + BC² = AC²

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2a97f94f336260c10b22191e6a8cb85c4c11c74656aa593af49a9a26c744ba32.png] 

The distance between the centre O and chord AB be x.

Then, The distance between the centre O and chord CD be (15 – x).

Now,

From ΔAMO,

AM² + OM² = OA²

⇒ (6)² + x² = r² ....(1)

Similarly from ΔOCN,

ON² + CN² = OC²

⇒ (15 – x)² + (9)² = r² ....(2)

From equation (1) and (2)

⇒ (6)2 + x2 = (15 – x)2 + (9)2 

⇒ 36 + x² = 225 + x² – 30x + 81

⇒ 30x = (225 – 36) + 81

⇒ 30x = (189 + 81)

⇒ 30x = 270

⇒ x = 9

Now, putting the value of x in equation (1), we get

⇒ (6)² + (9)² = r²

⇒ 36 + 81 = r²

⇒ 117 = r²

⇒ 3√13 = r

**∴ The value of radius is 3√13**

questions.question: ∆ABC, ∠A = 90°, M is the midpoint of BC and D is a point on BC such that AD⊥ BC. If AB = 7 cm and AC = 24 cm, then AD : AM is equal to:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5f54019e067cbeda919aaa334ccc40a8f39b432b55ba2f48d92cd66c85c0961f.png] 

In right angled ∆ABC, 90° at A

⇒ BC = √625 = 25

If, M is the midpoint of BC, then

AM = MC = BM = 25/2

As we know,

AD × BC = AB × AC

⇒ AD × 25 = 7 × 24

⇒ AD = (7 × 24)/25

∴ Ratio of AD : AM = (7 × 24)/25 : 25/2 = 336 : 625

questions.question: A circle touches the side BC of ΔABC at P and also touches AB and AC produced at Q and R, respectively. If the perimeter of ΔABC = 14.1 cm, then the length (in cm) of AQ will be:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A circle touches the side BC of ΔABC at P and also touches AB and AC produced at Q and R, respectively.

The perimeter of ΔABC = 14.1 cm

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d640fd4754b17e3fff2873580c35de8c0b065af3e724b8dd682f86c9334b20a7.png] 

AQ = AR [Tangents]

BP = BQ [Tangents]

CP = CR [Tangents]

Perimeter of ΔABC = AB + BP + CP + AC

⇒ 14.1 = AB + BQ + CR + AC

⇒ 14.1 = AQ + AR

⇒ 14.1 = AQ + AQ

⇒ 14.1 = 2AQ

⇒ AQ = (14.1/2) cm

⇒ AQ = 7.05 cm

**∴ The length of AQ is 7.05 cm**

questions.question: From an external point A, two tangents AB and AC have been drawn to a circle touching the circle at B and C respectively. P and Q are points on AB and AC respectively such that PQ touches the circle at R. If AB = 11 cm, AP = 7 cm and AQ = 9 cm, then find the length of PQ (in cm).
questions.solution:
**Given:**

AB = 11 cm

AP = 7 cm

AQ = 9 cm

**Concept used:**

Tangents drawn from same external point are equal in lengths.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/39cd1a273480671d4b38c9e824b958afce66bde57f1c0d6602d289a5126a088c.png] 

Tangents drawn from same external point are equal in lengths.

AB = AC, BP = PR and CQ = RQ

⇒ AB = AC = 11 cm

⇒ BP = AB - AP = 11 - 7 = 4 cm

⇒ CQ = AC - AQ = 11 - 9 = 2 cm

⇒ BP + CQ = 4 + 2 = 6 cm 

⇒ BP + CQ = PR + RQ = 6 cm

⇒ PR + RQ = PQ = 6 cm

**So, the length of PQ is 6 cm.**

questions.question: AB is a chord of a circle with centre O and P is any point on the circle. If ∠APB = 112°, then what is the measure of ∠OAB ?
questions.solution:

Concept of the line segment of the circle

**Calculation:**

In the given figure,

∠APB = 112°

AB is a chord

We know if a chord makes x° on the major arc of the circle then it will make 2x° on the center.

So, ∠AOB = 224°

But angle cannot be greater than 180°

So angle is = 360 - 224

⇒ 136° 

AO = BO = radius of the circle

So,

∠OAB = 44/2 = 22°

**∴ The measure of ∠OAB is 22°**

questions.question: Two circles of radii 20 cm and 5 cm, respectively, touch each other externally at the point P, AB is the direct common tangent of those two circles of centres R and S, respectively. The length of AB is equal to:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Radii of two circles = 20 cm and 5 cm

AB is the direct common tangent

**Formula used:**

When two circles touches at a point externally 

Direct common tangent = 2sqrt{ r₁ r₂}

r₁ = Radius of 1st circle

r₂ = Radius of 2ⁿd circle

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3d139eae40d819675c5d9bc852334905d5ad16e8ec7d45a4adb9ef8f6cfac75c.png] 

Direct common tangent = 2sqrt{ r₁ r₂}

⇒ 2sqrt{20× 5}

⇒ 2sqrt{100}

⇒ 2 × 10

⇒ 20

⇒ AB = 20 cm

**∴ Length of AB is 20 cm.**

questions.question: Two parallel chords on the same side of the centre of a circle are 12 cm and 20 cm long and the radius of the circle is 5√13 cm. What is the distance between the chords?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length of the first chord = 12 cm

Length of the second chord = 20 cm

Radius of the circle = 5√13 cm

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2ed431c5f2b7efda01a6fa2fce18cf2e435451f2093ff8beca5645f5292c8d29.png] 

OB = OD = 5 √13 cm

AB = 12 cm, CD = 20 cm, AM = MB = 12/2 = 6 cm and CN = ND = 20/2 = 10 cm

In Δ MBO

OB2 = MB2 + MO2

⇒ (5 √13)2 = 62 + OM2

⇒ OM2 = 325 – 36 = 289

⇒ OM = √289 = 17

In Δ NDO

OD2 = ND2 + NO2

⇒ (5 √13)2 = 102 + NO2

⇒ ON2 = 325 – 100 = 225

ON = √225 = 15

As we know,

OM = MN + ON

⇒ 17 = MN + 15

⇒ MN = 17 – 15 = 2 cm

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**

questions.question: Chords AB and CD of a circle intersect externally at P. If CD = 11.6 cm, PD = 6.4 cm and PB = 7.2 cm, then AB (in cm) is equal to:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Chords AB and CD of a circle intersect externally at P.

CD = 11.6 cm

PD = 6.4 cm

PB = 7.2 cm

**Concept used:**

Using basic proportionality theorem,

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/24526f6530eed7c3e8e36c4f5f9667337595d824f31cbc64b09ccc6379e27375.png] 

Let the value of AB be x 

Then, PA = PB + AB

⇒ PA = (7.2 + x) cm

Again,

PC = PD + CD

⇒ PC = (6.4 + 11.6) = 18 cm

Now,

Using basic proportionality theorem,

PB × PA = PD × PC

⇒ 7.2 × (7.2 + x) = 6.4 × 18

⇒ 51.84 + 7.2x = 115.2

⇒ 7.2x = (115.2 – 51.84)

⇒ 7.2x = 63.36

⇒ x = (63.36/7.2)

⇒ x = 8.8 cm

**∴ The required value of AB is 8.8 cm**
